blocks.es_reference: 📖 Administración y Liderazgo — Unidad 4: Organización, estructura y delegación

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "And He Himself gave some to be... pastors and teachers, for the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ." — Ephesians 4:11-12 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Y él mismo dio a unos... pastores y maestros, a fin de perfeccionar a los santos para la obra del ministerio, para la edificación del cuerpo de Cristo." — Efesios 4:11-12 (RVG)

blocks.en: Introduction — From Vision to Structure
blocks.es_reference: Introducción — De la visión a la estructura

blocks.en: In Unit 3 we watched a vision come down from God, pass through prayer and planning, and become the people's own resolve to build. But a vision without structure is only a wish. The walls of Jerusalem were not rebuilt by enthusiasm alone; Nehemiah assigned families to specific sections, each with its task, and the work held together because it was organized. This unit takes up that practical labor: how a leader turns a God-given vision into a structure that can actually carry it, and how he learns the hardest discipline of leadership — not doing the work himself, but equipping and releasing others to do it. Structure and delegation are not the cold machinery of the business world imported into the church. Rightly understood, they are how the body of Christ was designed by God to function: many members, each with a gift, each doing its part, knit together and built up in love.
blocks.es_reference: En la Unidad 3 vimos una visión descender de Dios, pasar por la oración y la planificación, y volverse la resolución propia del pueblo para edificar. Pero una visión sin estructura es solo un deseo. Los muros de Jerusalén no se reconstruyeron por el entusiasmo solo; Nehemías asignó familias a secciones específicas, cada una con su tarea, y la obra se mantuvo unida porque estaba organizada. Esta unidad toma esa labor práctica: cómo un líder convierte una visión dada por Dios en una estructura que de veras pueda llevarla, y cómo aprende la disciplina más difícil del liderazgo — no hacer él mismo la obra, sino capacitar y soltar a otros para que la hagan. La estructura y la delegación no son la fría maquinaria del mundo de los negocios importada a la iglesia. Bien entendidas, son el modo en que Dios diseñó que funcionara el cuerpo de Cristo: muchos miembros, cada uno con un don, cada uno haciendo su parte, unidos y edificados en amor.

blocks.en: Structure Serves the Mission, Not Itself
blocks.es_reference: La estructura sirve a la misión, no a sí misma

blocks.en: Begin with a warning, because structure is a good servant and a terrible master. A church needs enough structure to carry its mission — clear roles, lines of responsibility, a way that decisions get made and work gets done — and a church with too little of it collapses into confusion, where everyone assumes someone else will do the thing and no one does. But structure exists for the mission, never the reverse. The moment the organization becomes an end in itself — meetings that produce only more meetings, committees that exist to protect their own importance, procedures that smother the very ministry they were meant to serve — the scaffolding has begun to crush the building. Healthy structure is like the skeleton in a body: strong enough to give the body shape and let it move, but never visible for its own sake, always in the service of the life it carries. So the leader asks of every structure not "Is this impressive?" but "Does this help God's people do the work God has given them?"
blocks.es_reference: Comience con una advertencia, porque la estructura es un buen siervo y un amo terrible. Una iglesia necesita suficiente estructura para llevar su misión — roles claros, líneas de responsabilidad, una manera de tomar decisiones y hacer la obra — y una iglesia con muy poca se desploma en confusión, donde cada uno supone que otro hará la cosa y nadie la hace. Pero la estructura existe para la misión, nunca al revés. En el momento en que la organización se vuelve un fin en sí misma — reuniones que solo producen más reuniones, comités que existen para proteger su propia importancia, procedimientos que ahogan el mismo ministerio que debían servir — el andamio ha comenzado a aplastar el edificio. La estructura sana es como el esqueleto en un cuerpo: bastante fuerte para darle forma y dejarlo moverse, pero nunca visible por sí mismo, siempre al servicio de la vida que sostiene. Así que el líder pregunta de cada estructura no "¿Es impresionante?" sino "¿Ayuda esto al pueblo de Dios a hacer la obra que Dios le ha dado?"

blocks.en: The Goal of Structure: Equipping the Saints
blocks.es_reference: La meta de la estructura: perfeccionar a los santos

blocks.en: Now we reach the heart of the matter, and it is one verse that overturns how most people imagine ministry. Paul says that Christ gave leaders to the church — "for the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ" (Ephesians 4:11-12). Read that slowly, because the punctuation of how we live it makes all the difference. The leaders are not given to do all the ministry while the saints watch. The leaders are given to equip the saints, so that the saints do the work of ministry, and the whole body is built up. The pastor is a trainer of ministers, not the sole minister. When a church believes that ministry is the paid leader's job and the people's job is to attend, it has read this verse exactly backwards, and it will stay weak no matter how gifted the leader is, because the body was never meant to be carried by one organ. But where leaders equip and release the saints, every member becomes a minister, and the church can do a hundred times what one man could ever do alone.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora llegamos al corazón del asunto, y es un solo versículo que trastorna el modo en que casi todos imaginan el ministerio. Pablo dice que Cristo dio líderes a la iglesia — "a fin de perfeccionar a los santos para la obra del ministerio, para la edificación del cuerpo de Cristo" (Efesios 4:11-12). Léalo despacio, porque cómo lo vivimos cambia todo. Los líderes no fueron dados para hacer todo el ministerio mientras los santos miran. Los líderes fueron dados para perfeccionar a los santos, de modo que los santos hagan la obra del ministerio, y todo el cuerpo sea edificado. El pastor es un capacitador de ministros, no el único ministro. Cuando una iglesia cree que el ministerio es la tarea del líder pagado y que la tarea del pueblo es asistir, ha leído este versículo exactamente al revés, y quedará débil por dotado que sea el líder, porque el cuerpo nunca fue hecho para ser llevado por un solo órgano. Pero donde los líderes capacitan y sueltan a los santos, cada miembro se vuelve ministro, y la iglesia puede hacer cien veces lo que un solo hombre podría hacer solo.

blocks.en: "...for the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ." — Ephesians 4:11-12 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "...a fin de perfeccionar a los santos para la obra del ministerio, para la edificación del cuerpo de Cristo." — Efesios 4:11-12 (RVG)

blocks.en: Delegation Is Not Dumping
blocks.es_reference: Delegar no es deshacerse

blocks.en: If equipping is the goal, delegation is the method — and here many leaders fail, because they confuse delegation with dumping. Dumping is handing someone an unwanted task with no training, no authority, and no support, and then blaming them when it goes wrong. Delegation is something far higher. To delegate well is to entrust a real responsibility to a capable person, give them the authority to actually carry it, provide what they need to succeed, and then hold them lovingly accountable for the result. Recall Jethro's counsel to Moses from Unit 1: choose "able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness" and set them over the people (Exodus 18:21). Moses kept the weightiest matters but truly handed the rest over — not the appearance of authority, but the real thing. The leader who delegates only tasks while clutching all authority has not delegated at all; he has merely made others into his hands while keeping all the deciding to himself, and he will exhaust both them and himself. Real delegation gives away genuine responsibility to people equipped to bear it.
blocks.es_reference: Si perfeccionar es la meta, delegar es el método — y aquí muchos líderes fallan, porque confunden delegar con deshacerse de algo. Deshacerse es entregar a alguien una tarea no deseada sin capacitación, sin autoridad y sin apoyo, y luego culparlo cuando sale mal. Delegar es algo mucho más alto. Delegar bien es confiar una responsabilidad verdadera a una persona capaz, darle la autoridad para de veras llevarla, proveerle lo que necesita para tener éxito, y luego pedirle cuentas con amor por el resultado. Recuerde el consejo de Jetro a Moisés de la Unidad 1: escoger "varones de virtud, temerosos de Dios, varones de verdad, que aborrezcan la avaricia" y ponerlos sobre el pueblo (Éxodo 18:21). Moisés retuvo los asuntos más graves pero de veras entregó el resto — no la apariencia de autoridad, sino la cosa real. El líder que delega solo tareas mientras se aferra a toda la autoridad no ha delegado en absoluto; solo ha hecho de otros sus manos mientras se queda con todas las decisiones, y agotará a ellos y a sí mismo. La verdadera delegación entrega responsabilidad genuina a personas capacitadas para llevarla.

blocks.en: The apostles themselves show the pattern under pressure. When the daily distribution to the widows was being neglected and the complaints grew, they did not simply work longer hours and try to do it all; nor did they declare the task beneath them. They said, in effect, it is not right that we should leave the ministry of the Word to serve tables, and so they had the people choose seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and wisdom, and they handed the work over to them (Acts 6:2-4). Notice that they delegated real responsibility to capable, godly men, and that they did so precisely in order to guard their own God-given priority of prayer and the Word. Delegation is not only how the work gets covered; it is how a leader stays faithful to the few things only he can do, by entrusting to others the many things he need not do himself.
blocks.es_reference: Los apóstoles mismos muestran el patrón bajo presión. Cuando la distribución diaria a las viudas estaba siendo descuidada y crecían las quejas, no se limitaron a trabajar más horas tratando de hacerlo todo; ni declararon la tarea indigna de ellos. Dijeron, en efecto, que no era justo que dejaran el ministerio de la Palabra para servir a las mesas, y así hicieron que el pueblo escogiera siete varones de buen testimonio, llenos del Espíritu y de sabiduría, y les entregaron la obra (Hechos 6:2-4). Note que delegaron responsabilidad real a hombres capaces y piadosos, y que lo hicieron precisamente para guardar su propia prioridad dada por Dios de la oración y la Palabra. La delegación no es solo cómo se cubre la obra; es cómo un líder permanece fiel a las pocas cosas que solo él puede hacer, confiando a otros las muchas que no necesita hacer él mismo.

blocks.en: Let me tell you a story. It did not happen to one man exactly — but I have seen its two endings many times. A pastor planted a church and, because he was gifted and willing, did everything himself: he preached, he counseled, he led every meeting, he locked the doors at night. For a few years it worked, and people praised how hard he worked. But the church never grew past the size of one man's reach, and the people stayed spiritual infants, because they were never given anything to carry. Then he fell ill for three months — and the church nearly died, because everything had lived in him alone. A second pastor in the same situation did the opposite. From the start he gave ministry away: he trained teachers, raised up deacons, entrusted real work to faithful members and let them make real decisions. He looked, at first, less impressive — others were doing what people expected him to do. But his church grew strong and deep, and when he was gone for three months, it did not falter, because the ministry lived in the whole body and not in him. One man built a ministry around himself. The other built a body that could stand without him. Only one of them was obeying Ephesians 4.
blocks.es_reference: Déjeme contarle una historia. No le sucedió a un solo hombre exactamente — pero he visto sus dos finales muchas veces. Un pastor plantó una iglesia y, porque era dotado y dispuesto, lo hacía todo él mismo: predicaba, aconsejaba, dirigía cada reunión, cerraba las puertas de noche. Por unos años funcionó, y la gente alababa lo duro que trabajaba. Pero la iglesia nunca creció más allá del alcance de un solo hombre, y la gente siguió siendo niños espirituales, porque nunca se le dio nada que llevar. Luego él enfermó por tres meses — y la iglesia casi murió, porque todo había vivido en él solo. Un segundo pastor en la misma situación hizo lo contrario. Desde el principio regaló el ministerio: capacitó maestros, levantó diáconos, confió obra verdadera a miembros fieles y los dejó tomar decisiones verdaderas. Al principio parecía menos impresionante — otros hacían lo que la gente esperaba de él. Pero su iglesia se hizo fuerte y profunda, y cuando estuvo ausente tres meses, no se tambaleó, porque el ministerio vivía en todo el cuerpo y no en él. Un hombre edificó un ministerio alrededor de sí mismo. El otro edificó un cuerpo que podía sostenerse sin él. Solo uno de ellos obedecía Efesios 4.

blocks.en: Entrust to Faithful People
blocks.es_reference: Confiar a personas fieles

blocks.en: To whom should a leader delegate? Not simply to whoever is available or eager, but to those proven trustworthy, for the wrong steward can do more harm than an unfilled role. Paul gives Timothy the standard in a single, dense sentence: "And the things that you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also" (2 Timothy 2:2). Notice the two qualities Paul names. First, faithful — reliable, trustworthy, the kind of person who finishes what they begin and can be counted on when no one is watching. Second, able to teach others also — capable, and able to pass it on. And notice the reach of that one verse: Paul taught Timothy, Timothy is to commit it to faithful men, and those men will teach others also — four generations of ministry in a single breath. This is the seed of multiplication we will follow much further in a later unit. For now, the principle for structure and delegation is plain: build your church not around your own two hands, but by entrusting the work to faithful, capable people who will themselves equip still others.
blocks.es_reference: ¿A quién debe delegar un líder? No simplemente a quien esté disponible o entusiasmado, sino a los probadamente dignos de confianza, porque el mayordomo equivocado puede hacer más daño que un puesto vacío. Pablo le da a Timoteo la norma en una sola frase densa: "Y lo que has oído de mí ante muchos testigos, esto encarga a hombres fieles que serán idóneos para enseñar también a otros" (2 Timoteo 2:2). Note las dos cualidades que Pablo nombra. Primera, fieles — confiables, dignos de confianza, la clase de persona que termina lo que empieza y con quien se puede contar cuando nadie observa. Segunda, idóneos para enseñar también a otros — capaces, y capaces de transmitirlo. Y note el alcance de ese solo versículo: Pablo enseñó a Timoteo, Timoteo ha de encargarlo a hombres fieles, y esos hombres enseñarán también a otros — cuatro generaciones de ministerio en un solo aliento. Esta es la semilla de la multiplicación que seguiremos mucho más en una unidad posterior. Por ahora, el principio para la estructura y la delegación es claro: edifique su iglesia no alrededor de sus propias dos manos, sino confiando la obra a personas fieles y capaces que ellas mismas capacitarán aún a otros.

blocks.en: "...commit these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also." — 2 Timothy 2:2 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "...esto encarga a hombres fieles que serán idóneos para enseñar también a otros." — 2 Timoteo 2:2 (RVG)

blocks.en: The Courage to Release
blocks.es_reference: El valor de soltar

blocks.en: One thing remains, and it is more a matter of the heart than of organizational charts: the courage to actually let go. Many a leader designs a fine structure and recruits faithful people and then cannot bring himself to release control — he hovers, he overrides, he redoes the work others have done, and slowly teaches everyone that their efforts do not really matter. Such a leader has the form of delegation without its substance, and his people will eventually stop trying. To release others is an act of humility and faith: humility, because it means the work will be done differently than you would do it, and sometimes less well at first; faith, because it trusts that God gifts and uses His people, not only the leader. Remember that the same Spirit who called and gifted you has called and gifted them. A church can only ever grow as large as its leader is willing to release, for a church built around one man is forever limited to the size of one man. But a church where the leader equips the saints, delegates real responsibility to faithful people, and has the courage to release them — that church becomes what Ephesians describes: a whole body, joined and knit together, every part doing its share, growing and building itself up in love.
blocks.es_reference: Queda una cosa, y es más asunto del corazón que de organigramas: el valor de de veras soltar. Muchos líderes diseñan una buena estructura y reclutan personas fieles y luego no logran soltar el control — rondan, anulan, rehacen la obra que otros han hecho, y poco a poco enseñan a todos que sus esfuerzos en realidad no importan. Tal líder tiene la forma de la delegación sin su sustancia, y su gente con el tiempo dejará de intentar. Soltar a otros es un acto de humildad y de fe: humildad, porque significa que la obra se hará de modo distinto a como usted la haría, y a veces menos bien al principio; fe, porque confía en que Dios dota y usa a su pueblo, y no solo al líder. Recuerde que el mismo Espíritu que lo llamó y lo dotó a usted los ha llamado y dotado a ellos. Una iglesia solo puede crecer tanto como su líder esté dispuesto a soltar, porque una iglesia edificada alrededor de un solo hombre queda para siempre limitada al tamaño de un solo hombre. Pero una iglesia donde el líder perfecciona a los santos, delega responsabilidad verdadera a personas fieles, y tiene el valor de soltarlas — esa iglesia llega a ser lo que describe Efesios: un cuerpo entero, bien concertado y unido, cada parte haciendo su parte, creciendo y edificándose a sí mismo en amor.

blocks.en: "...from whom the whole body, joined and knit together by what every joint supplies... causes growth of the body for the edifying of itself in love." — Ephesians 4:16 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "...de quien todo el cuerpo, bien concertado y unido entre sí por todas las coyunturas... recibe su crecimiento para ir edificándose en amor." — Efesios 4:16 (RVG)

sa.prompt: Explain the proper relationship between structure and mission in the church.

A church needs enough structure to carry its work — clear roles and lines of responsibility — and too little of it collapses into confusion. sa.prompt: What does Ephesians 4:11-12 teach about the leader's true role, and what error does it correct?
sa.model: Ephesians 4:11-12 teaches that Christ gave leaders to equip the saints for the work of ministry, so that the saints do the ministry and the whole body is built up. The leader's true role is to be a trainer of ministers, not the sole minister. This corrects the common error of believing that ministry is the paid leader's job while the people's job is merely to attend; that reads the verse exactly backwards. The body was never meant to be carried by one organ, so a church organized that way stays weak no matter how gifted the leader. Where leaders equip and release the saints, every member becomes a minister and the church does far more than one man ever could.

sa.prompt: Distinguish true delegation from 'dumping,' and describe what good delegation includes.
sa.model: Dumping is handing someone an unwanted task with no training, no authority, and no support, then blaming them when it fails. True delegation is far higher: it entrusts a real responsibility to a capable person, gives them the authority to actually carry it, provides what they need to succeed, and then holds them lovingly accountable for the result. Moses did this on Jethro's counsel, keeping the weightiest matters but truly handing the rest over with real authority. A leader who delegates tasks while clutching all authority has not delegated at all; he has only made others his hands while keeping every decision, exhausting both them and himself. Good delegation gives away genuine responsibility to people equipped to bear it.

sa.prompt: According to 2 Timothy 2:2, to whom should ministry be entrusted, and why those qualities?
sa.model: Paul tells Timothy to commit what he has heard to faithful men who will be able to teach others also. Ministry should be entrusted to people who are faithful — reliable and trustworthy, finishing what they begin and dependable when no one watches — and able to teach others also — capable, and able to pass the work on. These qualities matter because the wrong steward can do more harm than an unfilled role, and because the goal is not merely to fill a slot but to multiply: Paul to Timothy, Timothy to faithful men, those men to others also — four generations in one verse. Entrusting the work to faithful, capable people who will equip still others is how the church grows beyond the leader's own reach.

sa.prompt: Why is the courage to release others an act of humility and faith?
sa.model: Releasing others is an act of humility because it means the work will be done differently than the leader would do it, and sometimes less well at first; the leader must surrender control and accept that his way is not the only good way. It is an act of faith because it trusts that God gifts and uses His people, not only the leader — the same Spirit who called and gifted the leader has called and gifted them. A leader who cannot release hovers, overrides, and redoes others' work, teaching everyone that their efforts do not matter, so they stop trying. But the leader who releases faithful people trusts God to work through the whole body, and only such release lets a church grow beyond the size of one man.

sa.prompt: Use the illustration of the two pastors to show the cost of failing to delegate.
sa.model: The first pastor did everything himself — preaching, counseling, leading every meeting — and for a time people praised his hard work. But his church never grew past the reach of one man, the people stayed spiritual infants because they were given nothing to carry, and when he fell ill for three months the church nearly died, because everything had lived in him alone. The second pastor gave ministry away from the start, training teachers, raising deacons, and entrusting real work and real decisions to faithful members. He looked less impressive at first, but his church grew strong and deep, and when he was gone three months it did not falter, because the ministry lived in the whole body. The cost of failing to delegate is a church that cannot outlive or outgrow its leader; only one of the two was obeying Ephesians 4.

sa.prompt: What are the dangers of BOTH too little and too much structure?
sa.model: Too little structure leaves a church in confusion, where everyone assumes someone else will do the task and no one does, so the work falls through the cracks. Too much structure, or structure that becomes an end in itself, smothers the very ministry it was meant to serve: meetings produce only more meetings, committees protect their own importance, and procedures choke the work — the scaffolding crushing the building. The healthy balance is enough structure to carry the mission but no more, always tested by whether it helps God's people do the work He has given them. Structure is a good servant and a terrible master, so it must stay in the service of the church's life and never rule over it.

sa.prompt: How does the body imagery of Ephesians 4:16 shape how a church should be organized?
sa.model: Ephesians 4:16 pictures the church as a body in which the whole grows as every joint supplies its part, building itself up in love. This shapes how a church should be organized: not as one organ doing everything while the rest are idle, but as many members, each with a gift, each doing its share. Organization and delegation exist to give every part its proper work, so that the body functions as God designed. A church organized around the body image equips and releases its members rather than centralizing all ministry in the leader, and the result is a church that grows and builds itself up in love because every part is supplying what it was gifted to supply.

sa.prompt: How does the divine/human pattern appear in equipping and delegation?
sa.model: The divine/human pattern appears in that God works His ministry through gifted human members rather than through the leader alone. It is divine because the same Spirit gifts and calls the saints, distributing abilities throughout the body as He wills; the gifts are God's doing, not the leader's invention. It is human because those gifts must be equipped, trained, and released through the leader's diligent work of teaching and entrusting. The leader does not manufacture the gifting, but he must develop and deploy it. So equipping the saints joins God's gifting with the leader's labor, exactly as Scripture's pattern runs: God accomplishes His purpose through prepared human means, and the leader's task is to ready and release the people God has gifted.

sa.prompt: Summarize Unit 4: how should a leader turn vision into a structure that lasts?
sa.model: Unit 4 teaches that a leader turns vision into a lasting structure by building not around his own two hands but around an equipped, released body. First, he provides enough structure to carry the mission, keeping it a servant and never a master. Second, he embraces the goal of Ephesians 4: to equip the saints for the work of ministry rather than to do it all himself. Third, he delegates truly — entrusting real responsibility and authority to faithful, capable people, as Paul charged Timothy to commit the work to faithful men able to teach others also. Finally, he finds the humility and faith to release them, trusting the Spirit who gifted them. The result is a body, joined and knit together, every part doing its share and building itself up in love — a church that can outgrow and outlast its leader.
